description_en: Located in the eastern part of the ancient settlement of Sunāguṭhī, the Bālakumārī Pīṭha occupies an extensive open ground locally known asdeykhyaḥ, a Newari term meaning “the field of the deity” or “the communal field of the settlement.” Within this wide meadow, partially covered by a wooded area, stands a single-storeyed pagoda-style temple—the principal shrine of Bālakumārī, the tutelary goddess (kṣetrapāla) of the Sunāguṭhī inhabitants. The entire meadow, including the adjacent cremation ground (masāna), forms the sacredpīṭha-complex. Architecturally, the temple is a simple square structure with a pyramidal roof, representing a relatively recent reconstruction although thepīṭhaitself may date back to the medieval period.In the 1960s CE (VS 2020s), the earlier temple, also a one-storeyed brick-and-tile structure, was destroyed when a large tree beside thepīṭhacollapsed upon it, resulting in the tragic death of a young girl inside. The present temple was rebuilt thereafter through local voluntary labor (śramadāna) and community donations. As aŚāktashrine, the wooden framework and door are ornamented with carvings ofŚāktadeities, and an elaborately carved woodentoraṇacrowns the entrance. The roof is covered with sheets of copper, while two metaldhvajas(banners) rise beside thegajūra(pinnacle), with smaller metalpatāḥs(pendants) hanging along the roof edges. Inside the sanctum, several uncarved stones represent the abstract presence of deities; among them, the central stone—adorned with a canopy of leaves—is revered as Bālakumārī, while the remaining stones are regarded as her attendantŚāktadeities.Unlike mostŚākta pīṭhas, which are open-air and templeless, Bālakumārī Pīṭha has long been associated with a constructed shrine. Though temples built atoppīṭhasare attested as early as the medieval period, they were generally open structures without doors. Elder residents recall that the earlier temple was also a small, square brick structure roofed with traditionaljhigāṭītiles (local resident, Mahārjana, male, age 82). No inscription precisely dates the original erection of the temple; however, the earliest extant record from the site dates to 1674 CE (NS 795). The inscription states that “stonedevalas(shrines) were constructed on both sides and completed, and thepātro(ritual stone container) of this stone was dedicated.” It begins with an invocation to theiṣṭadevatāand records the construction of two stone shrines, indicating that the text does not refer to the construction of the temple itself. In Newar society,degudyaḥ(ancestral household deities) are often callediṣṭadevatā. Thus, it appears that aŚākyafamily who regardedBāl Kumārīas theiriṣṭadevatāconstructed small stone shrines and offered the stonepātra(SUN0260-004).Another inscription dated 1871 CE (NS 991) mentions that “a stone was placed in thepīṭha-area.” The use of the termpīṭha-kṣetra(“thepīṭhaprecinct”) rather thanmandira-kṣetra(“temple precinct”) suggests that a substantial temple structure did not yet exist at that time. In recent decades, however, the formerly openpīṭha-ground has increasingly been encroached upon by concrete buildings,phalchās(resting pavilions), and subsidiary shrines, reducing its earlier openness.Ritual responsibility for Bālakumārī Pīṭha is shared among six members of the Sunāguṭhī community, who performnityapūjā(daily worship) in monthly rotation. Unlike mostpīṭhas, which hold a single annualkhaṭa-jātrā(procession), this shrine is exceptional for celebrating two such festivals each year. The first, known asChakhaḥ Jātrā, takes place in the month ofMaṅsira(November–December). On the full-moon night, the icon from the innerdyaḥchẽ(SUN0230) is placed upon akhaṭaand brought in procession to thepīṭha. Along withBāl Kumārī, masks of other deities are also arranged upon the abstractpīṭhastones, and a nocturnaltāntrika pūjāinvolving goat sacrifice is performed. During this ritual, a special bread calledchapātyāmariis distributed among devotees, who gather in large numbers to light lamps throughout the night. The following day, the images are again placed upon thekhaṭa, paraded back to the settlement, and communal feasting—known asdeybhvay—is held. This festival is also referred to as Chakhaḥ Jātrā or Atahaḥ Jātrā.The second festival of Bālakumārī occurs in the month of Caitra (March–April). On the 14th night of bright fortnight of Caitra, thekhaṭabearing the goddess is brought to thepīṭha, worshipped, and then returned to the settlement. This procession features fourkhaṭas—those of Gaṇeśa, Mahādeva, Kumāra, and Bālakumārī—and is thus known as Pyakhaḥ Jātrā (“the four-khaṭaprocession”). In nearby Ṭhecho, the traditionalŚāktadance-drama known asGathupyakhaṃis performed annually; every twelve years, the dancers’ costumes andmukuṇḍas(masks) are renewed in a ritual conducted at this verypīṭha, marking the formal re-inauguration of the performance. Within the broaderNavarātriobservance, on the day ofSaptamī, offerings of sparrows, pigeons, snakes, and buffalo are made into the fire ritual (havana), followed by the renewal of costumes and masks (local resident, Mahārjana, male, age 69).
description_ne: प्राय सबै पीठमा सम्बन्धित बस्तीको एकैमात्र खटजात्रा हुनेमा यहाँ भने अपवादका रूपमा यहाँ बालकुमारीको प्रतिवर्ष दुई पटक खटजात्रा हुने गर्दछ ।सुनागुथिमा प्राचीनवस्तीको पूर्वतिर ठुलो क्षेत्रफलमा फैलिएको चौर छ जसलाई स्थानीय भाषामा देय्‌ख्यः भनिन्छ । देय्‌ख्यःको अर्थ देवताको चौर वा देश (बस्ती) चौर भन्ने हुन्छ । ठुलो चौरमाझ केही भाग जङ्गल छ र सो जङ्गलमाझ एकतले पेगोडा मन्दिर खडा छ । यो मन्दिर सुनागुथिवासीका आरध्यदेवी अर्थात् क्षेत्रपाल बालकुमरीको पीठ हो र आसपासको समग्र चौर पीठक्षेत्र हो । पीठसँगै यहाँ मसान पनि आवद्ध छ । वर्गाकार स्वरूपमा उठाई छानो हालिएको मन्दिर सामान्य प्रकृतिको छ । पीठ कम्तिमा मध्यकालीन भए तापनि पीठमाथि बनेको मन्दिर त्यति पुरानो हैन । विसं २०२० को दशकमा पीठसँगैको विशाल रूख ढली पहिले भएको एकतले मन्दिर भत्किएको थियो । सो दुर्घटनामा मन्दिरभित्र एक बालिकाको पनि मृत्यु भएको थियो । तत् पश्चात् स्थानीयको श्रमदान र चन्दा संकलनबाट वर्तमान मन्दिर उठाइको हो । शाक्त मन्दिर भएकाले मन्दिरमा शाक्त देवदेवी कुँदिएका छन् । मन्दिरको मोहोडामा बुट्टेदार काँठको ढोका एवं तोरण चढाइको छ । छानामा तामाको पाता मोडिएको छ भने गजुरका साथमा धातुकै एकजोडा ध्वज खडा छन् । गजूरबाट छानोको किनारसम्म पुग्ने धातुका पताः लट्काइएका छन् । मन्दिरभित्र पीठका रूपमा अमूर्त ढुङ्गाहरू लहरै छन् । बीचको ढुङ्गालाई छेपुको तोरण हाली महत्व दिइएको छ । यही ढुङ्गालाई बालकुमरी मानिन्छ भने अन्य ढुङ्गालाई विविध शाक्त देवदेवी मानिन्छ ।प्रया शाक्त पीठहरू मन्दिरहीन खुला आकाशमुनि हुन्छन् । मध्यकालमै पीठमाथि मन्दिर उठाइएका केही उदाहरण पाइन्छन् तर ती पनि ढोका नहाली खुला छाडिएका देखिन्छन् । यहाँ वर्तमान मन्दिर पूर्वको (रुखबाट क्षति पुगेको) मन्दिर पनि स्वरूपमा वर्गाकार, इँट र झिंगटीको प्रयोग भएको सामान्य प्रकृतिको हुने गरेको भनाई यहाँका वृद्धहरू बताउछन् (local resident, Maharjana, male, age 82) । यहाँ पीठमाथि मन्दिर सुरुमा कहिले उठाइयो भन्ने तथ्य निश्चय गर्न सकिने कुनै अभिलेख प्राप्त छैन । यहाँ प्राप्त सर्वप्राचीन अभिलेख नेसं ७९५ (सन् १६७४) को हो । यस अभिलेखमा “दायाँ-बायाँ ढुङ्गाको देवल बनाई पूर्णता दिइयो र यो ढुङ्गाको पात्रो चढाइयो” भनिएको छ । यस अभिलेखको उठानमा इष्टदेवतालाई नमन गरिएको छ र दुईवटा ढुङ्गाका देवल बनाइयो भनिएको छ । यसबाट यो पीठमाथि मन्दिर बनेको अर्थमा लेखिएको अभिलेख नभएको देखिन्छ । नेवार समाजमा देगुद्यःलाई इष्टदेवता भनिएका उदाहरण पाइन्छन् । बालकुमारीलाई इष्टदेवता मान्ने कुनै शाक्य परिवारले साना ढुङ्गाका देवल बनाई यो ढुङ्गाको पात्र (SUN0260-004) चढाएको देखिन्छ । यहाँ अर्को एक अभिलेख छ जुन नेसं ९९१ (सन् १८७१) को हो । यस अभिलेखमा ‘पीठक्षेत्रमा ढुङ्गा बच्छाइयो” भनिएको छ । मन्दिर अगाडि वा मन्दिरक्षेत्र नभनी ‘पीठक्षेत्र’ भनिएबाट उक्त समयसम्म यहाँ ठुलो आकारका मन्दिर बनी नसेकेको प्रतीत हुन्छ । वर्तमानमा यो पीठ वरपरको खुला स्थानमा क्रमश कंक्रिड भवन, फल्चा एवं अन्य देवदेवीका देवलहरू (shrine) थपिँदै गई चौरको खुलापन हराउँदै गएको आभास हुन्छ ।यस बालकुमारी पीठमा सुनागुथिका छजना सदस्यले एक-एक महिनाको फरकमा पालैपालो नित्यपूजा गर्ने थिति छ । अन्य नेवार बस्तीका पीठमा एकैमात्र जात्रा हुनेमा यहाँ भने अपवादका रूपमा प्रतिवर्ष दुई पल्ट जात्रा मनाइन्छ । पहिलो जात्रालाई छखःजात्रा भनिन्छ जुन मंसिर  महिनामा हुने गर्दछ । मंसिर पूर्णिमाको रातमा बस्तीभित्र द्यःछेँ (SUN0230) मा रहेको मूर्तिलाई खटमा राखी यस पीठमा ल्याइन्छ । बालकुमारी मूर्तिका साथमा सबै देवदेवीका मुखाकृति पीठको अमूर्त ढुङ्गामाथि चढाई बोको बलि सहितको तान्त्रिक पूजा रातभर चल्छ । यस पूजाका दौरान छपात्यामरि नामक विशेष रोटी भक्तालुलाई बाढिन्छ । यस रात पीठमा दीयो बाल्ने भक्तालुको ठुलो घुँइचो लाग्छ । भोलिपल्ट मूर्ति एवं मुखाकृति पुनः खटमा चढाई बस्ती भित्र्याई जात्रा गरिन्छ र बस्तीका सबैले भोज खाने चलन छ जसलाई देय्‌भ्वय् भनिन्छ । यसलाई छखःजात्रा र अतःजात्रा पनि भन्ने चलन छ । बालकुमारीको अर्को जात्रा चैत्र महिनामा हुन्छ । खटमा राखिएको बालकुमारीलाई चैत्र शक्ल चतुर्दशीको रात पीठमा ल्याई पूजा गरी पुनः बस्तीमा फर्काइन्छ । यस जात्रामा अन्य तीन खट (गणेश, महादेव र कुमार) पनि हुन्छन् । कुल चार खट हुने भएबाट यसलाई प्यखःजात्रा (चार खटे जात्रा) भनिएको हो । ठेचोमा परम्परागत शाक्त देवदेवीको नाच हुने गर्दछ जसलाई गथुप्याखं भनिन्छ । प्रतिवर्ष निकालिने उक्त नृत्यमा १२ वर्षमा वस्त्र र मुकुण्डो फेर्ने थिति छ । मुकुण्डो र वस्त्र फेर्ने कार्य यसै पीठमा सम्पन्न गरी नृत्यको नव-प्रारम्भ यहीबाट गर्ने थिति छ । नवरात्री अन्तर्गत सप्तमीका दिन भँगेरा, परेवा, सर्प र राँगाको मासु हवन गरी वस्त्र र मुकुण्डो परिवर्तन गर्ने थिति छ (local resident, Maharjana, male, age 69) ।

historical_events.event_name: Construction of stone shines and offering of a stone vessel
historical_events.event_description: Two brothers of the Śākya lineage, Hākuju and Vinaju, constructed two small stone shrines (devala) and offered stone vessels (pātra) to their tutelary deities (iṣṭadevatā).

The sons of Śaṅkhamuni, Rājmāna and Mānasiṁha, together with all their family members, paved the ground of thepīṭhaarea with stone slabs. At the same time, during thejātrā, the spot in the settlement where the palanquin halts (capāḥkva) was also paved with stone.
An unidentified individual offered a bell (ghaṇṭa) in the name of Bālakumārī. The inscription on the bell records a date, but the donor’s name is not mentioned.
Ratna Bahādura Maharjana offered a woodentoraṇaabove the temple door.
Under the supervision of the Bālakumārī Protection and Renovation Group, the inner sanctum (garbhagṛha) of the temple was tiled through voluntary labor (śramadāna) and fundraising contributions.

historical_events.event_name: Covering the roof with metal sheet
historical_events.event_description: The roofing of the temple with copper sheets and the installation of ornamented struts were accomplished through voluntary labor and community donations. This restoration project was jointly undertaken by the Bālakumārī MāīRoof Renovation Committee and the Sāmudāyika Rupāntaraṇa Saṅgha–Nepāla.
Siddhi Bahādura Maharjana, in memory of his parents, offered apatāḥ(ritual banner) to the temple on the occasion of the Chakhaḥ Jātrā.
Rameśvarī, her son Bhīmsena, and Candramāyā, along with others, offered a bell (ghaṇṭa) in front of the temple in memory of their deceased family members.
The family of Kṛṣṇabhakta Maharjana offered a bell in front of the temple in memory of their departed ancestors.
Vilāpati Maharjana (Akhaḥ) offered apatāḥto the temple. The inscription on thepatāḥdoes not mention the date.
